findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "check_security_headers" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Security headers score 0–10: CSP, HSTS, framing, cookies, TLS. GET /x402/secscore?url= — $0.01.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "order_webmcp_upgrade" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: DESTRUCTIVE: places a paid WebMCP upgrade order ($4.00). Fetches the site and generates webmcp.js. Confirm with the user before calling. POST /x402/webmcp-upgra…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_security_headers, check_x402, lint_protocol_card, check_email_dns, get_page_roast, get_youtube_video, get_youtube_transcript, lookup_podcast, get_podcast_transcript, get_ats_job_detail · Private data: get_crypto_prices · Public sink: check_email_dns, order_webmcp_upgrade, classify_text, extract_keywords · Destructive: run_seo_audit, get_podcast_transcript.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_security_headers, check_x402, lint_protocol_card, check_email_dns, get_page_roast, get_youtube_video, get_youtube_transcript, lookup_podcast, get_podcast_transcript, get_ats_job_detail · Private data: get_crypto_prices · Public sink: check_email_dns, order_webmcp_upgrade, classify_text, extract_keywords · Destructive: run_seo_audit, get_podcast_transcript

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_webmcp" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "WebMCP agent-compatibility check with pass/fail verdict. GET /x402/webmcp-check?host= — $0.10." → after: "WebMCP compatibility check: what an agent sees on your site's tool surface, per-tool findings and the agent-ready verdict. GET /x402/webmcp-check?host= — $0.10."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
